title: CA-495(a) STILL OPEN, zero lines changed since round 9: the G22b scratch tree is created under the system temp directory at :7700 and removed on NO path -- a whole-file grep for tmp_g22b returns exactly three hits (:7700, :7701, :7702), none a removal; :7699 clears all four trap dispositions and the tree is not under $TMP so the top-level trap at :25 does not own it. Leaks on the SUCCESS path every run: run-all.sh auto-discovers the suite and CI runs the aggregator twice per pipeline. Its character-for-character identical G22a sibling at :7669 DOES carry the tail removal at :7683, so this is a dropped line, not a project pattern. False-alarm filter fails all three clauses. Fix: change the template root at :7700 from ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} to $TMP and leave :7699 untouched, so the parent trap reclaims it on every path.

CA-495(b) STILL OPEN, all eleven sites unchanged: scratch trees at :5542, :5580, :5616, :5643, :5668, :5708, :5757, :5812, :5961, :7669 and :8252 are rooted at ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} instead of the suite's own $TMP scratch root, inside subshells that correctly clear all four inherited trap dispositions and then leave a tail-position rm as the sole cleanup for a resource that now has no handler at all. Two concrete abort paths: sourcing edm-state re-enables errexit inside these subshells so a regression in edm-state aborts before the tail rm, and a Ctrl-C leaks these eleven while the parent trap reclaims the ~45 nested siblings, with :7669 additionally leaving a mode-555 directory. Fix: change the template root to $TMP at all eleven sites, keep every trap - line, keep the tail removals as a fast path; then add a bin/tests tripwire, since the T61 AC11 sweep at :1139 filters /tests/ out and is structurally blind to this class.

CA-481(a) STILL OPEN, byte-identical: the self-test fixture created at :147 is armed with trap 'rm -f "${tmp:-}"' RETURN EXIT INT TERM -- omits HUP and resumes instead of exiting on a real signal. This is now the single declared exception to a declared plugin-wide rule: bin/edm-check-grants:124-134 states the four-signal set EXIT INT TERM HUP with signal-shaped exits as the convention and nine sibling sites were converted. Fix: EXIT cleanup-only, INT then exit 130, TERM then exit 143, HUP then exit 129, keeping RETURN on the EXIT-equivalent arm.

CA-481(b) STILL OPEN: cmd_compare's first staging file is created at :758 but the cleanup traps arm only at :760-763, leaving a one-statement untrapped window. The die path IS covered (:759 carries an inline rm -f "$_CMP_TA"), so the residual exposure is a signal delivered between :758 and :760 -- small, which holds this at P2/medium. Fix: arm trap 'rm -f "$_CMP_TA"' EXIT INT TERM HUP immediately after :758, superseded by the two-file trap at :760.

CA-481(c) NEVER LANDED: no cross-file trap-convention assertion exists anywhere in bin/tests/. A grep of plugins/edm/bin/tests/ for CA-446|CA-447 returns zero hits. The plugin-wide four-signal convention is therefore stated in exactly one comment in one file (bin/edm-check-grants:124-134) and enforced nowhere. Fix: one assertion scanning bin/, bin/tests/ and evals/ for cleanup-trap lines, asserting each names HUP and each real-signal arm exits after cleanup, with a planted positive control.

CA-480 re-verified STILL OPEN on L3's axis but explicitly NOT an L5 finding. On L5's own axis the orphan is harmless: both .lockd and its .stale.$$ aside are matched by root .gitignore:36 and by the per-initiative ignore file, so a bricked lockdir never surfaces in git status. Its impact is availability, not hygiene.

CA-169 confirmed intact and must stay unapplied: with_state_lock deliberately never unlinks the flock lockfile because mutual exclusion is keyed on the inode, and both entry points write .edm-state.lock* into the per-initiative .gitignore. Do not fix in a later round.

Flock timeout marker verified clean, no finding: derived under TMPDIR not the tracked initiative directory, pre-cleared, mkdir only on the timeout branch, removed before the die. Its shared-/tmp predictable-PID-name exposure is an L8 axis already tracked under CA-305/CA-347.

write_atomic's staging files verified fully ignore-covered across every live destination; no .jsonl destination passes through write_atomic today so the absent *.jsonl.tmp.* pattern is currently unreachable -- worth a comment, not a finding.
evals/runs/ verified self-ignoring and retention-managed via prune_old_runs from all four exit paths. CA-066, CA-188, CA-214, CA-291 and CA-292 all confirmed fixed here.

--out DIR pointed at an unignored in-repo directory would deposit untracked run output, but this is deliberate and pruning of a caller-chosen root requires an explicit EDM_EVAL_PRUNE_EXPLICIT_OUT=true opt-in. Operator choice, not a defect.
CA-171 re-verified unchanged and still bounded: tiny files under TMPDIR with inline rm -f and no trap, on a path whose assertion helpers never exit early. Holding at NOTED rather than re-filing.
The hundreds of *.tmp-plus-mv pairs across wave6-smoke.sh all write inside the suite's own $TMP tree, which the four-signal trap at :34 owns. Correct by construction, no finding.
hooks.json creates no runtime files of its own -- every hook body delegates to a bin/ helper whose temp handling is audited above. Nothing to report on this lens.

edm-state update-patterns mutating tracked files inside the installed plugin directory is the intended Living-Library design and its staging path is covered by root .gitignore:16. Not a hygiene defect.
